whatItDoes: Performs date arithmetic and computes the exact duration between two dates. Add or subtract days, weeks, months, or years from a start date, and view the resulting date plus a day-of-week calendar preview. Also calculates the precise difference (years, months, days, hours, minutes) between any two dates.
whyItExists: Date math is deceptively tricky — months and years have uneven lengths, and adding 'one month' can land on an invalid day. A dedicated calculator removes the ambiguity and produces correct calendar arithmetic every time.
whoShouldUse: Project managers planning milestones, developers computing deadlines and durations, HR teams handling leave and tenure, and anyone tracking event or payment schedules.
useCases: Add 90 days to a contract start date to find the expiry date
Compute the number of days between two project milestones
Subtract months from a delivery date to set a planning deadline
Show a countdown or time-remaining summary between two dates
instructions: Choose the start date using the date picker
Select Add or Subtract and enter an amount in days, weeks, months, or years
Read the resulting date and its day of the week
For a difference, pick two dates and view the span in years, months, days, and time
Copy the result for use in schedules or documentation
examples: Start 2026-01-31, add 1 month → 2026-03-03 (clamped to February's end)
bestPractices: Verify month-end clamping behavior before relying on recurring dates
Use the difference tool for spans that need an exact breakdown
Cross-check leap-year and month-end cases in your own calculations
Treat results as calendar dates, not wall-clock times
Always specify whether '1 month' means calendar months or 30 days
commonMistakes: Assuming adding one month always lands on the same day of the month
Forgetting that date arithmetic is calendar-based, not duration-based
Confusing week starts and including the start day twice
Ignoring daylight saving time when combining dates and times
Using duration math (30 days) when you mean calendar arithmetic (1 month)
faq: How does adding a month handle month-end? — Adding one month to January 31 lands on February 28 (or 29), since the target day is clamped to the last valid day.
Is this intentional-shift arithmetic? — Yes, it follows natural calendar addition rather than elapsed-time arithmetic.
Does it handle leap years? — Yes, February dates account for leap years automatically.
Is anything sent to a server? — No, all computations run locally in your browser.
features: Add or subtract days, weeks, months, and years
Exact date difference with full breakdown
